fields.label: Layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting controls the height (and thus the total number) of the slices/layers. Thinner layers give better accuracy but take more time to print.

fields.label: First layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: When printing with very low layer heights, you might still want to print a thicker bottom layer to improve adhesion and tolerance for non perfect build plates.

fields.label: Perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This option sets the number of perimeters to generate for each layer. Note that Slic3r may increase this number automatically when it detects sloping surfaces which benefit from a higher number of perimeters if the Extra Perimeters option is enabled.

fields.label: Spiral vase
fields.upstreamHelp: This feature will raise Z gradually while printing a single-walled object in order to remove any visible seam. This option requires a single perimeter, no infill, no top solid layers and no support material. You can still set any number of bottom solid layers as well as skirt/brim loops. It won't work when printing more than one single object.

fields.label: Top solid layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of solid layers to generate on top surfaces.

fields.label: Bottom solid layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of solid layers to generate on bottom surfaces.

fields.label: Minimum top shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of top solid layers is increased above top_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of top shell. This is useful to prevent pillowing effect when printing with variable layer height.

fields.label: Minimum bottom shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of bottom solid layers is increased above bottom_solid_layers if necessary to satisfy minimum thickness of bottom shell.

fields.label: Extra perimeters if needed
fields.upstreamHelp: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

fields.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs (Experimental)
fields.upstreamHelp: Detect overhang areas where bridges cannot be anchored, and fill them with extra perimeter paths. These paths are anchored to the nearby non-overhang area when possible.

fields.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers).

fields.label: Avoid crossing curled overhangs (Experimental)
fields.upstreamHelp: Plan travel moves such that the extruder avoids areas where the filament may be curled up. This is mostly happening on steeper rounded overhangs and may cause a crash with the nozzle. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

fields.label: Avoid crossing perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Optimize travel moves in order to minimize the crossing of perimeters. This is mostly useful with Bowden extruders which suffer from oozing. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

fields.label: Avoid crossing perimeters - Max detour length
fields.upstreamHelp: The maximum detour length for avoid crossing perimeters. If the detour is longer than this value, avoid crossing perimeters is not applied for this travel path. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path.

fields.label: Detect thin walls
fields.upstreamHelp: Detect single-width walls (parts where two extrusions don't fit and we need to collapse them into a single trace).

fields.label: Thick bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

fields.label: Detect bridging perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Experimental option to adjust flow for overhangs (bridge flow will be used), to apply bridge speed to them and enable fan.

fields.label: Seam position
fields.upstreamHelp: Position of perimeters starting points.

fields.label: Seam gap distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

fields.label: Staggered inner seams
fields.upstreamHelp: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

fields.label: Scarf joint placement
fields.upstreamHelp: Where to place scarf joint seam.

fields.label: Scarf joint only on smooth perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Only use the scarf joint when the perimeter is smooth.

fields.label: Scarf start height
fields.upstreamHelp: Start height of the scarf joint specified as fraction of the current layer height.

fields.label: Scarf joint around entire perimeter
fields.upstreamHelp: Extend the scarf around entire length of the perimeter.

fields.label: Scarf joint length
fields.upstreamHelp: Length of the scarf joint.

fields.label: Max scarf joint segment length
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum length of any scarf joint segment.

fields.label: Scarf joint on inner perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Use scarf joint on inner perimeters.

fields.label: External perimeters first
fields.upstreamHelp: Print contour perimeters from the outermost one to the innermost one instead of the default inverse order.

fields.label: Fill gaps
fields.upstreamHelp: Enables filling of gaps between perimeters and between the inner most perimeters and infill.

fields.label: Perimeter generator
fields.upstreamHelp: Classic perimeter generator produces perimeters with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces perimeters with variable extrusion width. This setting also affects the Concentric infill.

fields.label: Fuzzy Skin
fields.upstreamHelp: Fuzzy skin type.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fields.upstreamHelp: The maximum distance that each skin point can be offset (both ways), measured perpendicular to the perimeter wall.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fields.upstreamHelp: Perimeters will be split into multiple segments by inserting Fuzzy skin points. Lowering the Fuzzy skin point distance will increase the number of randomly offset points on the perimeter wall.

fields.label: Single perimeter on top surfaces
fields.upstreamHelp: Use only one perimeter on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern. Could be applied on topmost surface or all top surfaces.

fields.label: Only one perimeter on first layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Use only one perimeter on the first layer.

fields.label: Fill density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of internal infill, expressed in the range 0% - 100%.

fields.label: Fill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Fill pattern for general low-density infill.

fields.label: Length of the infill anchor
fields.upstreamHelp: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

fields.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
fields.upstreamHelp: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. PrusaSlicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter. Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring.

fields.label: Top fill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Fill pattern for top infill. This only affects the top visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

fields.label: Bottom fill pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Fill pattern for bottom infill. This only affects the bottom external visible layer, and not its adjacent solid shells.

fields.label: Enable ironing
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable ironing of the top layers with the hot print head for smooth surface

fields.label: Ironing Type
fields.upstreamHelp: Ironing Type

fields.label: Flow rate
fields.upstreamHelp: Percent of a flow rate relative to object's normal layer height.

fields.label: Spacing between ironing passes
fields.upstreamHelp: Distance between ironing lines

fields.label: Automatic infill combination
fields.upstreamHelp: This feature automatically combines infill of several layers and speeds up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus maintaining accuracy.

fields.label: Automatic infill combination - Max layer height
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum layer height for combining infill when automatic infill combining is enabled. Maximum layer height could be specified either as an absolute in millimeters value or as a percentage of nozzle diameter. For printing with different nozzle diameters, it is recommended to use percentage value over absolute value.

fields.label: Combine infill every n layers
fields.upstreamHelp: This feature allows to combine infill and speed up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus accuracy.

fields.label: Solid infill every
fields.upstreamHelp: This feature allows to force a solid layer every given number of layers.

fields.label: Fill angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Default base angle for infill orientation. Cross-hatching will be applied to this. Bridges will be infilled using the best direction Slic3r can detect, so this setting does not affect them.

fields.label: Solid infill threshold area
fields.upstreamHelp: Force solid infill for regions having a smaller area than the specified threshold.

fields.label: Bridging angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for all bridges. Use 180° for zero angle.

fields.label: Only retract when crossing perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Disables retraction when the travel path does not exceed the upper layer's perimeters (and thus any ooze will be probably invisible).

fields.label: Infill before perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This option will switch the print order of perimeters and infill, making the latter first.

fields.label: Skirt Loops
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of loops for the skirt. If the Minimum Extrusion Length option is set, the number of loops might be greater than the one configured here. Set this to zero to disable skirt completely.

fields.label: Distance from brim/object
fields.upstreamHelp: Distance between skirt and brim (when draft shield is not used) or objects.

fields.label: Skirt height
fields.upstreamHelp: Height of skirt expressed in layers.

fields.label: Draft shield
fields.upstreamHelp:
With draft shield active, the skirt will be printed skirt_distance from the object, possibly intersecting brim.
Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object.
Limited = skirt is as tall as specified by skirt_height.
This is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft.

fields.label: Minimal filament extrusion length
fields.upstreamHelp: Generate no less than the number of skirt loops required to consume the specified amount of filament on the bottom layer. For multi-extruder machines, this minimum applies to each extruder.

fields.label: Brim type
fields.upstreamHelp: The places where the brim will be printed around each object on the first layer.

fields.label: Brim width
fields.upstreamHelp: The horizontal width of the brim that will be printed around each object on the first layer. When raft is used, no brim is generated (use raft_first_layer_expansion).

fields.label: Brim separation gap
fields.upstreamHelp: Offset of brim from the printed object. The offset is applied after the elephant foot compensation.

fields.label: Generate support material
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable support material generation.

fields.label: Auto generated supports
fields.upstreamHelp: If checked, supports will be generated automatically based on the overhang threshold value. If unchecked, supports will be generated inside the "Support Enforcer" volumes only.

fields.label: Overhang threshold
fields.upstreamHelp: Support material will not be generated for overhangs whose slope angle (90° = vertical) is above the given threshold. In other words, this value represent the most horizontal slope (measured from the horizontal plane) that you can print without support material. Set to zero for automatic detection (recommended).

fields.label: Enforce support for the first n layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Generate support material for the specified number of layers counting from bottom, regardless of whether normal support material is enabled or not and regardless of any angle threshold. This is useful for getting more adhesion of objects having a very thin or poor footprint on the build plate.

fields.label: First layer density
fields.upstreamHelp: Density of the first raft or support layer.

fields.label: First layer expansion
fields.upstreamHelp: Expansion of the first raft or support layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

fields.label: Raft layers
fields.upstreamHelp: The object will be raised by this number of layers, and support material will be generated under it.

fields.label: Raft contact Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The vertical distance between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface.

fields.label: Raft expansion
fields.upstreamHelp: Expansion of the raft in XY plane for better stability.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Style
fields.upstreamHelp: Style and shape of the support towers. Projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports, while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Top contact Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The vertical distance between object and support material interface. Setting this to 0 will also prevent Slic3r from using bridge flow and speed for the first object layer.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Bottom contact Z distance
fields.upstreamHelp: The vertical distance between the object top surface and the support material interface. If set to zero, support_material_contact_distance will be used for both top and bottom contact Z distances.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Pattern used to generate support material.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: With sheath around the support
fields.upstreamHelp: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Pattern spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing between support material lines.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Pattern angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Use this setting to rotate the support material pattern on the horizontal plane.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Closing radius
fields.upstreamHelp: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Top interface layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Bottom interface layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Number of interface layers to insert between the object(s) and support material. Set to -1 to use support_material_interface_layers

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Interface pattern
fields.upstreamHelp: Pattern used to generate support material interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Interface pattern spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing between interface lines. Set zero to get a solid interface.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Interface loops
fields.upstreamHelp: Cover the top contact layer of the supports with loops. Disabled by default.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Support on build plate only
fields.upstreamHelp: Only create support if it lies on a build plate. Don't create support on a print.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: XY separation between an object and its support
fields.upstreamHelp: XY separation between an object and its support. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%), it will be calculated over external perimeter width.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Don't support bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: Experimental option for preventing support material from being generated under bridged areas.

fields.group: Options for support material and raft
fields.label: Synchronize with object layers
fields.upstreamHelp: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

fields.label: Maximum Branch Angle
fields.upstreamHelp: The maximum angle of the branches, when the branches have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle to be able to have more reach.

fields.label: Preferred Branch Angle
fields.upstreamHelp: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

fields.label: Branch Diameter
fields.upstreamHelp: The diameter of the thinnest branches of organic support. Thicker branches are more sturdy. Branches towards the base will be thicker than this.

fields.label: Branch Diameter Angle
fields.upstreamHelp: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

fields.label: Branch Diameter with double walls
fields.upstreamHelp: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

fields.label: Tip Diameter
fields.upstreamHelp: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

fields.label: Branch Distance
fields.upstreamHelp: How far apart the branches need to be when they touch the model. Making this distance small will cause the tree support to touch the model at more points, causing better overhang but making support harder to remove.

fields.label: Branch Density
fields.upstreamHelp: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

fields.label: Perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for perimeters (contours, aka vertical shells). Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Small perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= 6.5mm (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: External perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This separate setting will affect the speed of external perimeters (the visible ones). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the perimeters speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing the internal fill. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing solid regions (top/bottom/internal horizontal shells). This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the default infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Top solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing top solid layers (it only applies to the uppermost external layers and not to their internal solid layers). You may want to slow down this to get a nicer surface finish. This can be expressed as a percentage (for example: 80%) over the solid infill speed above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Support material
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing support material.

fields.label: Support material interface
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing support material interface layers. If expressed as percentage (for example 50%) it will be calculated over support material speed.

fields.label: Bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing bridges.

fields.label: Over bridges
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for printing solid infill above bridges. Set to 0 to use solid infill speed. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over solid infill speed.

fields.label: Gap fill
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for filling small gaps using short zigzag moves. Keep this reasonably low to avoid too much shaking and resonance issues. Set zero to disable gaps filling.

fields.label: Ironing
fields.upstreamHelp: Ironing

fields.label: Enable dynamic overhang speeds
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting enables dynamic speed control on overhangs.

fields.label: speed for 0% overlap (bridge)
fields.upstreamHelp: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

fields.label: speed for 25% overlap
fields.upstreamHelp: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

fields.label: speed for 50% overlap
fields.upstreamHelp: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

fields.label: speed for 75% overlap
fields.upstreamHelp: Overhang size is expressed as a percentage of overlap of the extrusion with the previous layer: 100% would be full overlap (no overhang), while 0% represents full overhang (floating extrusion, bridge). Speeds for overhang sizes in between are calculated via linear interpolation. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over the external perimeter speed. Note that the speeds generated to gcode will never exceed the max volumetric speed value.

fields.label: Travel
fields.upstreamHelp: Speed for travel moves (jumps between distant extrusion points).

fields.label: Z travel
fields.upstreamHelp:
Speed for movements along the Z axis.
When set to zero, the value is ignored and regular travel speed is used instead.

fields.label: First layer speed
fields.upstreamHelp: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first layer, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

fields.label: First layer solid infill speed
fields.upstreamHelp: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed (for example: 40% of the solid infill speed). Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

fields.label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
fields.upstreamHelp: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

fields.label: External perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for external perimeters. Set zero to use the value for perimeters.

fields.label: Perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for perimeters. Set zero to disable acceleration control for perimeters.

fields.label: Top solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for top solid infill. Set zero to use the value for solid infill.

fields.label: Solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for solid infill. Set zero to use the value for infill.

fields.label: Infill
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for infill. Set zero to disable acceleration control for infill.

fields.label: Bridge
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for bridges. Set zero to disable acceleration control for bridges.

fields.label: First layer
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer.

fields.label: First object layer over raft interface
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

fields.label: Wipe tower
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for wipe tower. Set zero to disable acceleration control for the wipe tower.

fields.label: Travel
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will use for travel moves. Set zero to disable acceleration control for travel.

fields.label: Travel short distance acceleration
fields.upstreamHelp: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

fields.label: Default
fields.upstreamHelp: This is the acceleration your printer will be reset to after the role-specific acceleration values are used (perimeter/infill). Set zero to prevent resetting acceleration at all.

fields.label: Max print speed
fields.upstreamHelp: When setting other speed settings to 0 Slic3r will autocalculate the optimal speed in order to keep constant extruder pressure. This experimental setting is used to set the highest print speed you want to allow.

fields.label: Max volumetric speed
fields.upstreamHelp: This experimental setting is used to set the maximum volumetric speed your extruder supports.

fields.label: Max volumetric slope positive
fields.upstreamHelp: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from lower speed to higher speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 1.8 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 20 mm/s) to 5.4 mm³/s (feedrate 60 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

fields.label: Max volumetric slope negative
fields.upstreamHelp: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from higher speed to lower speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 5.4 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 60 mm/s) to 1.8 mm³/s (feedrate 20 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

fields.label: Perimeter extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing perimeters and brim. First extruder is 1.

fields.label: Infill extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing infill.

fields.label: Solid infill extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing solid infill.

fields.label: Support material/raft/skirt extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing support material, raft and skirt (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes).

fields.label: Support material/raft interface extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing support material interface (1+, 0 to use the current extruder to minimize tool changes). This affects raft too.

fields.label: Wipe tower extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

fields.label: Bed temperature by extruder
fields.upstreamHelp: The extruder which determines bed temperatures. Set to 0 to determine temperatures based on the first printing extruder of the first and the second layers.

fields.label: Enable
fields.upstreamHelp: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

fields.label: Temperature variation
fields.upstreamHelp: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is defined.

fields.label: Enable
fields.upstreamHelp: Multi material printers may need to prime or purge extruders on tool changes. Extrude the excess material into the wipe tower.

fields.label: Width
fields.upstreamHelp: Width of a wipe tower

fields.label: Wipe tower brim width
fields.upstreamHelp: Wipe tower brim width

fields.label: Maximal bridging distance
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

fields.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
fields.upstreamHelp: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

fields.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
fields.upstreamHelp: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

fields.label: Extra flow for purging
fields.upstreamHelp: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

fields.label: No sparse layers (EXPERIMENTAL)
fields.upstreamHelp: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

fields.label: Prime all printing extruders
fields.upstreamHelp: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

fields.label: Interface shells
fields.upstreamHelp: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

fields.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum width of a segmented region. Zero disables this feature.

fields.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
fields.upstreamHelp: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth"is bigger then "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

fields.label: Use beam interlocking
fields.upstreamHelp: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

fields.label: Interlocking beam width
fields.upstreamHelp: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

fields.label: Interlocking direction
fields.upstreamHelp: Orientation of interlocking beams.

fields.label: Interlocking beam layers
fields.upstreamHelp: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

fields.label: Interlocking depth
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

fields.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
fields.upstreamHelp: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

fields.label: Default extrusion width
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to allow a manual extrusion width. If left to zero, Slic3r derives extrusion widths from the nozzle diameter (see the tooltips for perimeter extrusion width, infill extrusion width etc). If expressed as percentage (for example: 230%), it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: First layer
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for first layer. You can use this to force fatter extrudates for better adhesion. If expressed as percentage (for example 120%) it will be computed over first layer height. If set to zero, it will use the default extrusion width.

fields.label: Perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for perimeters. You may want to use thinner extrudates to get more accurate surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%) it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: External perimeters
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for external perimeters. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 200%), it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: Infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. You may want to use fatter extrudates to speed up the infill and make your parts stronger. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: Solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for solid surfaces. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise 1.125 x nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: Top solid infill
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for infill for top surfaces. You may want to use thinner extrudates to fill all narrow regions and get a smoother finish. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: Support material
fields.upstreamHelp: Set this to a non-zero value to set a manual extrusion width for support material. If left zero, default extrusion width will be used if set, otherwise nozzle diameter will be used. If expressed as percentage (for example 90%) it will be computed over layer height.

fields.label: Automatic extrusion widths calculation
fields.upstreamHelp: Automatically calculates extrusion widths based on the nozzle diameter of the currently used extruder. This setting is essential for printing with different nozzle diameters.

fields.label: Infill/perimeters overlap
fields.upstreamHelp: This setting applies an additional overlap between infill and perimeters for better bonding. Theoretically this shouldn't be needed, but backlash might cause gaps. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over perimeter extrusion width.

fields.label: Bridge flow ratio
fields.upstreamHelp: This factor affects the amount of plastic for bridging. You can decrease it slightly to pull the extrudates and prevent sagging, although default settings are usually good and you should experiment with cooling (use a fan) before tweaking this.

fields.label: Slice gap closing radius
fields.upstreamHelp: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

fields.label: Slicing Mode
fields.upstreamHelp: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

fields.label: Slice resolution
fields.upstreamHelp: Minimum detail resolution, used to simplify the input file for speeding up the slicing job and reducing memory usage. High-resolution models often carry more detail than printers can render. Set to zero to disable any simplification and use full resolution from input.

fields.label: G-code resolution
fields.upstreamHelp: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

fields.label: Arc fitting
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. G-code resolution will be used as the fitting tolerance.

fields.label: XY Size Compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: The object will be grown/shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value (negative = inwards, positive = outwards). This might be useful for fine-tuning hole sizes.

fields.label: Elephant foot compensation
fields.upstreamHelp: The first layer will be shrunk in the XY plane by the configured value to compensate for the 1st layer squish aka an Elephant Foot effect.

fields.label: Perimeter transitioning threshold angle
fields.upstreamHelp: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of perimeters. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no perimeters will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center perimeters, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

fields.label: Perimeter transitioning filter margin
fields.upstreamHelp: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra perimeter and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum perimeter width - margin, 2 * Minimum perimeter width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Perimeter transition length
fields.upstreamHelp: When transitioning between different numbers of perimeters as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the perimeter segments. If expressed as a percentage (for example 100%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Perimeter distribution count
fields.upstreamHelp: The number of perimeters, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer perimeters don't change in width.

fields.label: Minimum perimeter width
fields.upstreamHelp: Width of the perimeter that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum perimeter width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the perimeter will become as thick as the feature itself. If expressed as a percentage (for example 85%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Minimum feature size
fields.upstreamHelp: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum perimeter width. If expressed as a percentage (for example 25%), it will be computed based on the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Complete individual objects
fields.upstreamHelp: When printing multiple objects or copies, this feature will complete each object before moving onto next one (and starting it from its bottom layer). This feature is useful to avoid the risk of ruined prints. Slic3r should warn and prevent you from extruder collisions, but beware.

fields.label: Verbose G-code
fields.upstreamHelp: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

fields.label: Label objects
fields.upstreamHelp:
Selects whether labels should be exported at object boundaries and in what format.
OctoPrint = comments to be consumed by OctoPrint CancelObject plugin.
Firmware = firmware specific G-code (it will be chosen based on firmware flavor and it can end up to be empty).

This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

fields.label: Output filename format
fields.upstreamHelp: You can use all configuration options as variables inside this template. For example: [layer_height], [fill_density] etc. You can also use [timestamp], [year], [month], [day], [hour], [minute], [second], [version], [input_filename_base], [default_output_extension].

fields.label: G-code substitutions
fields.upstreamHelp: Find / replace patterns in G-code lines and substitute them.

fields.label: Post-processing scripts
fields.upstreamHelp: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Slic3r config settings by reading environment variables.

fields.label: Configuration notes
fields.upstreamHelp: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

fields.label: Compatible printers condition
fields.upstreamHelp: A boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.
